stem: The mean of 4, 7, 9, 10 and 15 is
explanation: Mean = (4 + 7 + 9 + 10 + 15)/5 = 45/5 = 9. 45 is the total, which still has to be divided by the number of values.

stem: The median of 3, 8, 5, 12, 7 and 10 is
explanation: In order the values are 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12; with six values the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th, (7 + 8)/2 = 7.5. 8.5 averages the two middle values of the unsorted list (5 and 12), which is wrong because the data must be ordered first.

stem: The mode of the data 2, 4, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7 is
explanation: The mode is the most frequent value: 6 occurs three times, more than any other. 3 is how often the mode occurs, not the mode itself.

stem: The range of the data 12, 25, 7, 18, 30 is
explanation: Range = largest − smallest = 30 − 7 = 23. 18 subtracts the first value from the second-largest, and 37 adds the extremes instead of subtracting.

stem: The standard deviation of the data 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (taking the population standard deviation) is
explanation: The mean is 6 and the squared deviations are 16, 4, 0, 4, 16, totalling 40. Variance = 40/5 = 8, so SD = √8 = 2√2. 8 is the variance, which still needs a square root.

stem: A data set has mean 20 and standard deviation 4. If 5 is added to every value, the new mean and new standard deviation are
explanation: Adding a constant shifts every value, so the mean becomes 20 + 5 = 25, but the spread is unchanged and the SD stays 4. Adding 5 to the SD as well (giving 9) is the usual mistake.

stem: In an Islamabad college, section A has 30 students with a mean score of 60 and section B has 20 students with a mean score of 70. The mean score of all 50 students is
explanation: Combined mean = (30 × 60 + 20 × 70)/50 = (1,800 + 1,400)/50 = 3,200/50 = 64. 65 is the simple average of the two means, which ignores that section A is larger.

stem: The table shows the marks scored by 10 students in a quiz. The mean mark is
explanation: Mean = Σfx/Σf = (20 + 60 + 120 + 40)/10 = 240/10 = 24. 25 is the average of the four mark values, which ignores how many students got each mark.

stem: Ali has 4 shirts and 3 pairs of trousers. The number of different shirt-and-trousers outfits he can wear is
explanation: By the multiplication principle, 4 × 3 = 12 outfits. Adding (4 + 3 = 7) counts the items, not the pairings.

stem: In how many ways can 5 students stand in a row for a photograph?
explanation: The number of arrangements is 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120. 720 is 6!, and 25 is 5², which allows the same student in more than one place.

stem: How many three-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 if no digit is repeated?
explanation: There are 6 choices for the first digit, 5 for the second and 4 for the third: 6 × 5 × 4 = ⁶P₃ = 120. 216 = 6³ allows repetition, and 20 = ⁶C₃ ignores the order of the digits.

stem: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 8 people?
explanation: Order does not matter, so the number is ⁸C₃ = (8 × 7 × 6)/(3 × 2 × 1) = 56. 336 = ⁸P₃ counts ordered selections, as if the members held different posts.

stem: The number of different arrangements of all the letters of the word PAKISTAN is
explanation: PAKISTAN has 8 letters with A occurring twice, so the number is 8!/2! = 40,320/2 = 20,160. 40,320 treats the two A's as different letters.

stem: A team of 2 men and 2 women is to be chosen from 5 men and 4 women. The number of possible teams is
explanation: Men can be chosen in ⁵C₂ = 10 ways and women in ⁴C₂ = 6 ways, so there are 10 × 6 = 60 teams. 126 = ⁹C₄ ignores the 2-and-2 condition, and 16 adds the two counts instead of multiplying.

stem: A fair six-sided die is thrown once. The probability that it shows a prime number is
explanation: The primes on a die are 2, 3 and 5, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2. 1/3 forgets that 2 is prime, and 1 is not a prime number.

stem: A bag contains 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green marbles. One marble is taken at random. The probability that it is blue is
explanation: There are 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 marbles and 3 are blue, so P(blue) = 3/10. 3/7 compares blue with non-blue marbles (odds), not with the total.

stem: Three fair coins are tossed together. The probability of getting at least one head is
explanation: There are 2³ = 8 equally likely outcomes and only TTT has no head, so P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8. 1/8 is the probability of no head at all, the complement of the event asked for.

stem: Two fair dice are thrown. The probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 8 is
explanation: Of the 36 equally likely outcomes, (2, 6), (3, 5), (4, 4), (5, 3), (6, 2) give 8, so P = 5/36. 1/11 treats the 11 possible sums 2 to 12 as equally likely, which they are not.

stem: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5. The probability that A and B occur together is
explanation: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2. 0.7 is P(A or B) = 0.4 + 0.5 − 0.2, and 0.9 simply adds the probabilities.

stem: The probability that it will rain in Lahore tomorrow is 0.35. The probability that it will not rain is
explanation: P(not A) = 1 − P(A) = 1 − 0.35 = 0.65. 0.5 assumes rain and no rain are equally likely.

stem: A box contains 4 red and 6 white balls. Two balls are drawn one after the other without replacement. The probability that both are red is
explanation: P = 4/10 × 3/9 = 12/90 = 2/15, since after one red ball is removed only 3 red balls remain among 9. 4/25 = (4/10)² is the answer with replacement.

stem: One card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 playing cards. The probability that it is a king or a heart is
explanation: P(king or heart) = 4/52 + 13/52 − 1/52 = 16/52 = 4/13; the king of hearts is subtracted once because it was counted twice. 17/52 forgets this overlap.

stem: The mean of six numbers is 15. When one number is removed, the mean of the remaining five is 14. The number removed is
explanation: The total falls from 6 × 15 = 90 to 5 × 14 = 70, so the removed number is 90 − 70 = 20. Answering 1 uses only the change in the mean (15 − 14), not the change in the total.

stem: The table shows the monthly sales of a shop in Karachi. The percentage increase in sales from March to April is
explanation: Increase = 75 − 60 = 15 thousand, and 15/60 × 100 = 25%. 20% divides the increase by the April figure (15/75) instead of the earlier March figure.

stem: The table shows the number of children in 20 families. The median number of children is
explanation: With 20 families the median is the average of the 10th and 11th values. Cumulative frequencies are 3, 10, 14, …, so the 10th value is 2 and the 11th is 3, giving a median of 2.5. 2 is the mode, the most common value.

stem: The standard deviation of a set of values x is 3. The standard deviation of the values 2x + 5 is
explanation: Multiplying every value by 2 doubles the spread, while adding 5 does not change it, so the new SD is 2 × 3 = 6. 11 wrongly applies the +5 to the standard deviation, and 36 is the new variance.

stem: A student must answer 4 of the 7 questions on a paper, and question 1 is compulsory. The number of ways she can choose her questions is
explanation: Question 1 is fixed, so she chooses the other 3 from the remaining 6: ⁶C₃ = 20. 35 = ⁷C₄ ignores the compulsory question.

stem: A fair die is thrown twice. The probability of getting at least one six is
explanation: P(no six in two throws) = 5/6 × 5/6 = 25/36, so P(at least one six) = 1 − 25/36 = 11/36. 1/3 adds 1/6 + 1/6 and counts the double six twice; 5/18 = 10/36 is the chance of exactly one six.

stem: In how many ways can 6 friends be seated around a circular table, if only their positions relative to each other matter?
explanation: For a circular arrangement fix one person and arrange the rest: (6 − 1)! = 5! = 120. 720 = 6! counts the rotations of the same seating as different.

stem: A family in Multan spends Rs 60,000 a month. In a pie chart of its spending, the sector for rent has an angle of 90°. The monthly rent is
explanation: The rent's share is 90°/360° = 1/4, so the rent is 60,000 ÷ 4 = Rs 15,000. Rs 54,000 treats the 90 degrees as 90 per cent.
